messages:
maya: Heads-up — prod token tail latency spiked around 10:05 UTC. Not a full outage but p99 per-token jumped ~2x for some routes. Seeing correlation with kernel switches + KV miss storms. Anyone saw the same?

raj: saw the alert, pulled a short profile. Looks like the selection logic fell back to the generic "matmul_fallback" kernel for long sequences when memory pressure rose. That kernel has ~+15ms per token on 1024+ seqs.

anika: we rolled a small batching heuristics tweak last night (reduce max_batch_wait to 3ms on the low-latency bucket). Could've increased the number of small batches and changed kernel choice.

leo: also noticed a KV cache churn pattern — clients with long-prefetch sessions caused a burst of KV misses after the GC window. Miss-heavy paths routed to kernels that aren't optimized for kv_miss fallback.

ops-bot: deploy: rollout/2027-11-03/runtime-batching-tweak -> success :white_check_mark:

maya: packing these together: (1) batching tweak altered batch shapes, (2) kernel selector picked suboptimal kernels for those shapes, (3) KV misses amplified per-token latency. Needs both telemetry and a short-term mitigation.

raj: quick sample from profiler (trimmed):
```
{ kernel: "matmul_fallback", seq_len: 1536, batch_size: 2, kv_hit: false, token_ms: 34.8 }
{ kernel: "opt_kv_v3", seq_len: 512, batch_size: 8, kv_hit: true, token_ms: 11.2 }
```
Shows clear delta when kv_hit toggles.

anika: agree. If max_batch_wait reduced we get smaller batch_size median -> kernels optimized for bigger batch sizes lose perf. We should revert heuristic or gate it behind route-level SLOs.

leo: separate but related: billing reports for those routes show cost-per-token rose ~12% last 24h vs our internal cost model only showing ~5%. I suspect our token accounting doesn't account for kernel-level rework on misses (extra compute tokens) or for micro-retries.

sre-oncall: can we attach a trace id? i'll pull flamegraphs if you paste a few request ids. Also propose a temporary mitigation: prefer kernel "opt_kv_v3" when kv_hot_rate < 80% to avoid expensive fallbacks.

maya: good. Action items proposal: 
- emit per-token microevents (one event per produced token) with tags: kernel, kv_hit, batch_size, route, seq_len_bucket, token_ms, request_id, trace_id.
- add a derived metric: route_p95_token_ms and route_cost_per_token (internal) that sums kernel_compute_ms * cost_factor / tokens.
- reconcile billing by adding token_lineage events to billing pipeline (token_count_raw vs token_count_compute).

raj: implementation notes: keep sampling first (1/100 tokens) to avoid massive cardinality. For debug traces, allow opt-in full sampling per request_id. We'll add a compact protobuf for microevents to reduce churn.

anika: i'll own the dashboard. Plan: new Grafana folder "runtime/token_view" with panels:
- per-route p50/p95/p99 token_ms
- kernel split: bar by kernel showing avg token_ms and kv_hit rate
- batch_shape heatmap (batch_size x seq_len -> token_ms)
- cost per token rolling 24h (internal) vs billing pipeline metric
I'll wire alerts: route_p95_token_ms > 40ms for 10m -> paging.

leo: on billing side i'll add a transform that ingests token_lineage and outputs billing_aligned_token_count. We need to define exact mapping: compute_tokens = tokens_emitted + tokens_regenerated_on_kv_miss + tokens_from_retries. I'll draft the spec by EOD.

billing-bot: billing pipeline note: current aggregator uses ingress/egress counts from API gateway. It doesn't see intra-runtime recompute; recommend adding compute_token metric from runtime to the billing topic.

maya: agree. Owners: anika -> dashboard + alerts (this week), raj -> microevent proto + sampling (PR by Thu), leo -> billing transform spec (EOD) + follow-up (Mon), maya -> kernel selector guard (temporary hotfix) and coordinate rollback if needed.

raj: small perf regression hypothesis: the new batch_wait tweak improved cold-latency p50 for small routes but regressed tail on long sequence routes. We should run A/B with kernel preference AND original batching to measure.

anika: can we add a short-lived KPI: route_unit_economics (rolling 1h) = route_cost_per_token / route_success_rate to highlight routes losing dollars per successful token?

leo: yes — that'll help prioritize optimizations. Also add tags for customer_tier so we can see enterprise vs free tier economics.

maya: sounds good. I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow 09:30 UTC to review first dashboards and any hotfix. For now -> rollback batch_wait tweak to previous value on low-latency bucket (I'm going to send the rollback), and enable kernel preference guard tunable as discussed.

ops-bot: deploy: rollback/2027-11-03/runtime-batching-tweak -> success :white_check_mark: (maya)

mood: :thumbsup:
